en.title: GitHub Copilot is now available in JetBrains Air
en.summary: You can now delegate coding tasks, guide execution, and review results with GitHub Copilot in JetBrains Air . The integration uses the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) and supports tasks in your JetBrains IDE or in the cloud.
en.details:
You can now delegate coding tasks, guide execution, and review results with GitHub Copilot in JetBrains Air . The integration uses the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) and supports tasks in your JetBrains IDE or in the cloud.

Use Copilot in Air alongside the GitHub Copilot plugin and choose the workflow that works best for you. For a comparison and FAQ, see GitHub Copilot in JetBrains Air .

What’s new

- GitHub Copilot in Air’s agent picker : Select GitHub Copilot and use your existing Copilot subscription for coding tasks.

- Parallel work and in-context review : Track multiple agent sessions, use project context and IDE tools, and review changes alongside your code.

- Cloud tasks on your GitHub Copilot subscription : Run Copilot in isolated cloud environments through Air Teams, from your IDE or browser. Tasks use your Copilot plan rather than JetBrains AI credits.

Get started

For local tasks, install Air in your JetBrains IDE , select GitHub Copilot , and connect your GitHub Copilot account.

For cloud tasks, you’ll need a JetBrains account in an Air Teams-enabled business organization, a GitHub Copilot subscription, and Copilot enabled by your Air administrator. There are two ways to run cloud tasks:

- Browser : Open Air in your browser , connect GitHub under Settings > VCS Providers , and create a task. Choose your repository and remote branch, select GitHub Copilot , and send your prompt. …

en.title: AI Is Changing How Semiconductor Fabs Work — and Engineers Are Moving Faster Because of It
en.summary: Demand for advanced chips is rising. The processes to build them are getting more complex. And the margin for error is shrinking.
en.details:
Demand for advanced chips is rising. The processes to build them are getting more complex. And the margin for error is shrinking.

For engineers, understanding how a process change will behave, how a material will interact with a new step, how a defect maps back to a root cause are critical, challenging steps in semiconductor manufacturing — and these analyses can take days. Physical experiments on a fab line are slow and expensive. A wrong call on yield or process quality has real consequences.

AI is transforming semiconductor manufacturing, impacting what engineers can do — and how fast.

Accelerated computing shortens simulation time, allowing engineers to evaluate more alternatives before committing to physical trials.

Physics-based AI helps engineers predict process behavior without running a full simulation every time.

AI agents handle sequences of engineering tasks that once consumed hours.

And digital twins let teams test changes in a virtual environment before committing to physical trials.

Together, these capabilities describe an AI-defined fab: a semiconductor manufacturing factory where AI helps engineers optimize processes, catch problems earlier and make better decisions across the full manufacturing chip lifecycle. Engineers direct the work and make decisions based on their expertise while spending less time waiting for answers.

items.originalTitle: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI

en.title: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI
en.summary: Cities generate enormous amounts of data from cameras, sensors and operational systems, but turning it into useful action — for planning, maintenance and public services — remains a challenge.
en.details:
Cities generate enormous amounts of data from cameras, sensors and operational systems, but turning it into useful action — for planning, maintenance and public services — remains a challenge.

Physical and agentic AI offer new ways to close that gap, from digital twins for infrastructure planning to vision and service agents, while keeping local governments in control of how sensitive data is processed and used.

Building on initiatives announced at GTC Berlin , NVIDIA and its partners are expanding physical AI and AI agents to cities worldwide. Shared computing infrastructure gives city departments, neighboring municipalities and local developers a common foundation to build on — extending services without each organization having to acquire and manage resources of their own.

Agentic AI for Cities

From resident services to vision agents, cities are adopting NVIDIA agentic AI to deliver faster, more responsive public services. City teams don’t need a massive infrastructure investment to get started building these AI services: depending on the workload, NVIDIA RTX workstations or a small GPU system may be enough. …
